title: Self-host reconstruction spike + managed-bridge stand-up (ADR-0005)
summary: De-risk the reconstruction backend chosen in ADR-0005 (AUTH #018): build a self-hosted Gaussian-splat pipeline and, in parallel, stand up a managed bridge for early M1 validation. Prove a real captured room reconstructs and renders on a physical iPhone before committing the M1 pipeline. GPU long-running ops go to the Grok Operator; the pipeline code is the Builder's.
deliverables: services/reconstruction/ (self-host pipeline: COLMAP/GLOMAP + gsplat or Brush + Open3D)

acceptance_tests.test: The self-host pipeline produces a Gaussian splat (.ply/.spz) plus a derived collision mesh from a captured room, using only commercially-licensed components (gsplat/Splatfacto or Brush + COLMAP/GLOMAP + Open3D; INRIA 3DGS and SuGaR excluded). A report records the exact stack, licenses, and per-scan GPU time and cost.

The pruned/compressed splat renders on a physical iPhone in Unity 6 URP; splat count, package size, and frame rate are recorded against the <=150 MB package and 30 fps targets. Measurements are suggested evidence (SPEC 11), not a gate.

A managed reconstruction bridge is stood up for M1 validation and reconstructs at least one test scan: Autodesk APS Reality Capture (DPA in place) OR KIRI Engine only under a written no-train + DPA. The vendor's terms are filed in legal/vendors/ before any real user scan (SECURITY_CHECKLIST 6.3).
A decision note recommends self-host vs the managed bridge for the M1 pipeline, with the iOS splat-render risk assessed; it feeds an ADR-0005 addendum if the direction firms up.

history.event: created by the Coordinator as the ADR-0005 reconstruction follow-up (AUTH #018, Owner chose 'spike + bridge').
